flow.costPlain: The direct cost of delivering Arm's designs and support — tiny next to revenue, which is why gross margin is 95.6%. It includes $6M of share-based pay and $7M of related employer taxes, net of R&D tax incentives.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Designing new processors and platform technology; the GAAP figure includes $127M of share-based pay (paying staff in shares), $118M of related employer taxes net of R&D tax incentives, and $13M of a one-time employee benefit from settling the 2019 All Employee Plan. Engineering headcount rose 24% year over year.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling and running the company; the GAAP figure includes $53M of share-based pay and $38M of related employer taxes, plus $5M of the one-time 2019 All Employee Plan settlement benefit. Non-GAAP SG&A fell 26% year over year as share-based pay shifted from liability-settled to equity-settled and legal costs came in lower.

follow100Note: License ($44.61) and royalty ($55.39) revenue make up the $100. Direct costs took $4.42; R&D took $62.93 and SG&A $30.28 — together more than the gross profit, leaving just $2.37 before other items. Interest and other gains added $4.63, equity investments lost $0.75, and a $166M tax benefit added $17.89. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Arm beat its own Q4 guidance ($850–900M revenue); full-year FY24 revenue was $3,233M, up 21% year over year.

kpis.note: diluted, vs $0.00 a year ago; non-GAAP $0.36

kpis.label: Royalty revenue
kpis.note: +37% YoY — a record, on wider Armv9 adoption

oneTimers: Arm recorded a $166M windfall tax benefit tied to share-based pay: without it, net income would have been $58M instead of $224M. Excluding it (and share-based pay), non-GAAP net income was $376M.
Operating expenses include an $18M one-time employee benefit from settling the Arm Limited All Employee Plan 2019 ($13M in R&D, $5M in SG&A).
otherDetail: Other items added $36M: $30M of net interest income and a $13M other non-operating gain, partly offset by a $7M loss from equity investments. Tax was a $166M benefit — a windfall tied to share-based pay — so it added to profit instead of taking from it.
pngFooterNote: Record revenue; a $166M tax benefit powered the profit.

segments.name: License and other revenue
segments.note: Fees for licensing Arm chip designs, plus support and related services; up 60% YoY on multiple high-value long-term license agreements as companies invest in Arm-based technology for AI across all end markets, plus revenue from agreements signed in earlier quarters.

segments.name: Royalty revenue
segments.note: A cut of every chip shipped with Arm technology inside; up 37% YoY to a record as Armv9 chips — which command higher royalty rates — spread wider, with strong growth in smartphones (AI-enabled Armv9 handsets), custom chips from cloud hyperscalers, and automotive (driver assistance and digital cockpits). IoT/embedded dipped slightly on semiconductor weakness.

takeaways.text: Revenue rose 47% to a record $928M, above guidance ($850–900M), on record royalty revenue of $514M (+37%) and license revenue of $414M (+60%) from multiple high-value long-term deals. The pipeline looks strong too: remaining performance obligations were $2,484M (+45% YoY) and annualized contract value $1,182M (+15% YoY). Arm guided Q1 FY25 revenue of $875–925M and full-year FY25 revenue of $3,800–4,100M.
takeaways.title: Record revenue, above guidance

takeaways.text: Royalty revenue hit a record $514M as Armv9 chips, which carry higher royalty rates, spread into more markets: smartphone royalties grew strongly on AI-enabled Armv9 handsets, cloud hyperscalers' custom Arm-based chips gained share, and automotive royalties grew on driver-assistance and digital-cockpit chips. IoT/embedded dipped slightly on semiconductor weakness. Customers reported shipping 7.0 billion Arm-based chips in the December quarter, taking the cumulative total to 287.4 billion.
takeaways.title: Armv9 is lifting what Arm earns per chip

takeaways.text: GAAP operating profit was just $22M (a 2.4% margin) after $865M of operating expenses, swollen by $186M of share-based pay and $156M of related employer taxes as engineering headcount grew 24%. Non-GAAP operating profit was $391M, a 42.1% margin. Net income of $224M (vs $3M a year ago) was powered by a $166M windfall tax benefit tied to share-based pay — without it, profit would have been $58M. Free cash flow was $637M, and $907M over the trailing twelve months (+50% YoY).
takeaways.title: Thin operating profit — the tax benefit did the heavy lifting

verdict: Arm's revenue jumped 47% to a record $928M on record royalty revenue of $514M, and net income surged to $224M from $3M a year ago — though most of the profit came from a $166M tax benefit, not from operations.
